# Parts guide

**Generated by `tools/roles.py --write` from `tools/design.py` and the
text in `tools/roles.py`. Do not hand-edit; change the text there.**

What every part on the board is for. The same text is in the schematic
(hover a symbol, or read the paragraph in each dashed group box) and in
the PCB (select a footprint, Description field). Start with the sheet
you care about; within it, groups appear in schematic order.

- [FPGA](#fpga) (111 parts): The Artix-7 itself, its decoupling, how it boots and its clock.
- [Power](#power) (135 parts): Inputs, the regulators that make every rail, extension power protection.
- [Memory](#memory) (83 parts): Four PSRAM chips for working memory and the flash the FPGA boots from.
- [Supervisor](#supervisor) (74 parts): The RP2350B board controller: USB, power sequencing, programming the FPGA.
- [Slots](#slots) (98 parts): The ten extension ports: connectors, per-slot fuses, 5 V level shifting.
- [Network](#network) (39 parts): Gigabit Ethernet (PHY and jack) and the two raw LVDS link ports.
- [Video](#video) (8 parts): HDMI output straight from the FPGA, with its protection chip.

## FPGA

The Artix-7 itself, its decoupling, how it boots and its clock.

### U1  FPGA

The FPGA is the board: every user design (a NEORV32 RISC-V core, a video pipeline, a protocol bridge) runs here. Its six user I/O banks are dedicated by job: bank 13 at 1.8 V carries the four PSRAMs and the two 5 V bus translators, bank 14 the configuration flash, the board-controller sideband, the 50 MHz clock, the SDRAM address bus, the MRAM and the microSD socket, banks 15 and 34 the direct extension slots A-D and E-H at a jumper-selected voltage, bank 16 the network at 2.5 V, bank 35 the HDMI output, the SDRAM data bus and the PHY reset/interrupt. Ball-by-ball list: ref/ballmap.md; constraints: ref/freya.xdc.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | XC7A100T-2FGG676I | FPGA: Xilinx/AMD Artix-7 XC7A100T-2FGG676I: 101k logic cells, 4.9 Mb block RAM, 240 DSP slices. Runs whatever design you load; configures itself from U6 at power-on or is loaded by the board controller over JTAG. |

### config straps (UG470)

How the FPGA loads its design at power-on. M[2:0] = 001 selects master SPI: the FPGA clocks its bitstream out of the W25Q256 flash (U6) by itself. The mode straps are 1 k, the most UG470 v1.17 Table 2-4 allows. PROGRAM_B and INIT_B are pulled up so the board controller can restart configuration; PUDC_B is strapped high so the FPGA adds no pull-ups while it configures: every line that needs a level (PHY reset, SDRAM CS/CKE, MRAM and microSD CS, the 5 V bus OE, the PSRAM clock and data) has its own resistor, and nothing fights it. DONE lights D1 through Q4 once a design is running.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | F.0603.00025/P2-0603G1TS2-06T-002 | FPGA DONE LED: Green LED, lit once the FPGA has finished loading a design. |
| Q4 | BSS138LT1G | DONE LED driver: Small N-MOSFET that sinks D1's current when DONE goes high, so the LED never loads the FPGA's open-drain DONE pin. |
| R1 | 1k | 1k pull-up of CFG_M0 to +3V3, for U1 (FPGA): mode pin M0 = 1: master SPI boot (UG470 Table 2-4, at most 1 k) |
| R2 | 1k | 1k pull-down on CFG_M1, for U1 (FPGA): mode pin M1 = 0: master SPI boot (UG470 Table 2-4) |
| R3 | 1k | 1k pull-down on CFG_M2, for U1 (FPGA): mode pin M2 = 0: master SPI boot (UG470 Table 2-4) |
| R4 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of CFG_PROG_B to +3V3, for U1 (FPGA): keeps PROGRAM_B released; pulling it low restarts configuration |
| R5 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of CFG_INIT_B to +3V3, for U1 (FPGA): keeps INIT_B released; it goes low on a configuration error |
| R6 | 1k | 1k pull-up of PUDC_B to +3V3, for U1 (FPGA): PUDC_B high: no I/O pull-ups during configuration, the external resistors set every line (UG470) |
| R7 | 330 | 330 resistor from DONE_LED_A to +3V3, for D1 (FPGA DONE LED): sets D1's current |
| R98 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of CFG_DONE to +3V3, for Q4 (DONE LED driver) |

### GTP calibration

The XC7A100T has two quads of multi-gigabit transceivers (GTP). Rev A uses none of them, but UG482 Tables 5-5 and 5-6 still want their supplies powered, their receive inputs grounded and one 100 ohm 1 % calibration resistor per quad to MGTAVTT. These two resistors are that.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| R35 | 100 1% | 100 1% resistor from MGTRREF to +1V2_MGT, for U1 (FPGA): calibration resistor for GTP quad 216 (UG482 Figure 5-1) |
| R89 | 100 1% | 100 1% resistor from MGTRREF_213 to +1V2_MGT, for U1 (FPGA): calibration resistor for GTP quad 213 (UG482 Table 5-5) |

### X4 system clock

The FPGA's own clock. X4 runs at 50 MHz from power-on and enters bank 14 on a clock-capable (MRCC) ball, so it can feed an MMCM and make any frequency the design needs. Without it nothing in the fabric would run until a network link came up.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| X4 | 50MHz CMOS | 50 MHz FPGA clock: YXC OT322550MJBA4SL 50 MHz CMOS oscillator: the fabric's always-running clock (SYS_CLK), into a bank 14 MRCC ball. |
| C246 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +3V3, for X4 (50 MHz FPGA clock) |
| R147 | 33 | 33 series resistor between SYS_CLK and SYS_CLK_OSC, for X4 (50 MHz FPGA clock): damps ringing on the clock line |

### config flash

The FPGA's non-volatile memory. At power-on the FPGA reads its design (bitstream) from this 32 MB flash by itself (master SPI, set by the mode straps). The board controller can rewrite it through the series resistors on the Board Controller sheet, and spare space can hold user data or software for a soft CPU.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| R203 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of FLASH_CS_B to +3V3, for U6 (FPGA configuration flash) |

## Power

Inputs, the regulators that make every rail, extension power protection.

### input OR-ing

Where power enters. Two inputs feed one internal supply, VSYS: USB-C (5 V, or 9 V when a USB-PD charger agrees) and the J50 screw terminal (9-21 V). A diode on each (D3, D4) lets whichever is higher supply the board and stops one input from back-feeding the other. On the USB side, U26 is an electronic fuse: it ramps the voltage up gently so plugging in does not spark, cuts off above about 10 V or below 3.75 V, and limits current to about 2 A. D8 clamps voltage spikes on the screw input. VSYS then feeds the two main regulators.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| D3 | SS34 | USB input diode: SS34 Schottky diode: lets USB power reach VSYS and stops the screw input feeding back into USB. |
| D4 | SS34 | screw input diode: SS34 Schottky diode: lets the screw input reach VSYS and stops USB feeding back into it. |
| D8 | SMBJ22A | screw input surge clamp: SMBJ22A TVS diode: absorbs voltage spikes on the screw input above about 24 V. |
| J50 | 9-21V POWER IN | POWER IN screw terminal: Main power input, 9-21 V DC. Polarity marked on the board. |
| U26 | TPS259470ARPWR | USB input eFuse: TI TPS259470A: ramps USB power in gently, cuts off outside 3.75-10 V, limits current to about 2 A, blocks reverse current. Reports faults on EXT_FAULT. |
| C184 | 2.2nF 25V | 2.2nF 25V capacitor from VBUS_DVDT to GND, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets how slowly U26 ramps VSYS up, about 0.9 V/ms |
| C185 | 10uF 50V | 10uF 50V bypass on VSYS, for U26 (USB input eFuse) |
| C186 | 10uF 50V | 10uF 50V bypass on VSYS, for U26 (USB input eFuse) |
| C187 | 10uF 25V | 10uF 25V bypass on VBUS, for U26 (USB input eFuse) |
| R50 | 100k | 100k resistor from VBUS_UVLO to VBUS, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets U26's turn-on voltage, 3.75 V |
| R51 | 47k | 47k resistor from VBUS_UVLO to GND, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets U26's turn-on voltage, 3.75 V |
| R52 | 73.2k | 73.2k resistor from VBUS_OVLO to VBUS, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets U26's cut-off voltage, about 10 V |
| R53 | 10k | 10k resistor from VBUS_OVLO to GND, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets U26's cut-off voltage, about 10 V |
| R54 | 1.65k | 1.65k resistor from VBUS_ILM to GND, for U26 (USB input eFuse): sets U26's current limit, about 2 A |

### U11  VSYS to +5V

Switching regulator (buck converter) that makes +5V from VSYS. It runs whenever power is present (no enable), like U12, so the FPGA's 1.8 V auxiliary supply is never missing while its 3.3 V banks are powered. Its output goes to the +5V rail through U34. +5V feeds the 5 V buses, the extension 5 V pins and the four small regulators below. The two feedback resistors set the output voltage; the inductor and capacitors are its power stage; the 10 uF across its input is its own switching-current reservoir.

### extension power protection control

Shared control for the four protected extension supplies (U21-U24). EXT_EN, from the board controller, turns them all on; the pull-down keeps them off until firmware decides. EXT_FAULT is pulled up and goes low if any of them (or the USB eFuse) detects a fault, so one controller pin hears all of them.

| R73 | 10k | 10k pull-up of EXT_FAULT to +3V3, for U7 (board controller): shared fault line, low when a protected supply trips |

Protected switch between the board's +5V and the 5 V pins of every extension port. Limits current to about 1 A and blocks current flowing back from an extension. Without it, a shorted extension would pull the whole board's 5 V down.

### rail monitors

Lets the board controller measure every supply. Each rail goes to one of its eight analog inputs (ADC), which read 0-3.3 V. Rails at or below 3.3 V go through a 1 k resistor that protects the pin; VSYS and +5V are higher, so two resistors divide them down first. A 100 nF capacitor on each input steadies the reading. MON_1V8 reads +1V8 itself, the FPGA's VCCAUX behind the bead, so an open bead shows; the two jumpered domains are measured so firmware knows how J19/J20 are set. +1V2_MGT is the one rail not measured. Firmware uses this to check each regulator came up before enabling the next.

### AUX IN

### VCCAUX filter

The split between +1V8_IO and +1V8. VCCAUX and VCCADC are the FPGA's internal supplies (clocking, I/O pre-drivers, the XADC) and should not share copper with switching 1.8 V I/O loads, so they hang off U14's output through one ferrite bead (120 ohm at 100 MHz, 2 A, 50 mohm: 9 mV at the 0.18 A VCCAUX allowance, inside VCCAUX's 1.71 V minimum). The 10 uF and 100 nF sit at U14's output beside its own capacitors; VCCAUX keeps its UG483 decoupling on the +1V8 side.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| C261 | 10uF | 10uF bypass on +1V8_IO |
| C262 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +1V8_IO |
| FB1 | 120R 2A BLM18PG121SN1D | 120R 2A BLM18PG121SN1D resettable fuse feeding +1V8_IO from +1V8 |

### U34  +5V source select

Chooses what feeds the +5V rail: USB power straight from the connector, or U11. A regulator cannot make 5 V out of 5 V, so on a plain 5 V USB source the mux passes VBUS to the rail. It hands the rail to U11 while the board controller asks the charger for 9 V and for a few seconds after (Q6), while the screw input is powered (Q7), and, as a backstop, if VBUS rises above about 5.6 V unasked or goes away. The choice is wired, not firmware: dividers and two small transistors. The chip blocks current flowing backwards into either source, limits the rail current to about 2.5 A and ramps it up gently. ST tells the board controller which source is in use.

Blocks reverse current both ways, limits to about 2.5 A. |

### Q6  mux hold: 9 V request

Keeps U34 on U11 around a 9 V negotiation. The controller's 9 V request charges a capacitor through D24 at once and the capacitor drains through its resistor in 2-7 s, so the rail leaves VBUS before the charger moves it and returns only when VBUS is back at 5 V. No voltage threshold can do that within the tolerances involved.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| D24 | 1N4148W | mux hold diode: 1N4148W: charges the Q6 hold capacitor from PD_REQ_9V at once and lets it drain slowly through its own resistor. |
| Q6 | BSS138LT1G | mux: 9 V request hold: Small N-MOSFET that pulls U34's PR1 to ground while the board controller asks for 9 V and for 2-7 s after it stops (D24, R, C hold), so the +5V rail is on U11 before VBUS moves and until it is back at 5 V. |
| C279 | 10uF | 10uF capacitor from SEL_IN2 to GND, for Q6 (mux: 9 V request hold): Q6's gate: charged from PD_REQ_9V through D24, drains through 470k/10 uF in 2-7 s |
| R200 | 470k | 470k resistor from SEL_IN2 to GND, for Q6 (mux: 9 V request hold): Q6's gate: charged from PD_REQ_9V through D24, drains through 470k/10 uF in 2-7 s |

### Q7  mux hold: screw input present

Keeps U34 on U11 whenever the screw input carries voltage, so a bench supply on J50 carries the whole board even with a 5 V USB cable plugged in; before, the USB port kept the 5 V load.

| R201 | 100k | 100k series resistor between EXT_PRESENT and VIN_EXT, for J50 (POWER IN screw terminal): Q7's gate: 100k/33k from the screw input, on above 3.2-6 V of VIN_EXT |
| R202 | 33k | 33k pull-down on EXT_PRESENT, for Q7 (mux: screw input present): Q7's gate: 100k/33k from the screw input, on above 3.2-6 V of VIN_EXT |

### config flash

The FPGA's non-volatile memory. At power-on the FPGA reads its design (bitstream) from this 32 MB flash by itself (master SPI, set by the mode straps). The board controller can rewrite it through the series resistors on the Board Controller sheet, and spare space can hold user data or software for a soft CPU.

### SDRAM

A 32 MB SDR SDRAM (Winbond W9825G6KH-6, 16 bits wide, up to 166 MHz) for designs that outgrow the PSRAMs: a framebuffer, a soft CPU's main memory, a capture buffer. Its data and control lines come from bank 35 and its address lines from bank 14, both at 3.3 V. One 100 nF per VDD/VDDQ pin pair (seven, datasheet pins 1, 14, 27 and 3, 9, 43, 49) and a 10 uF bulk; a 22 ohm series resistor at the FPGA damps the clock; CS is pulled up and CKE pulled down so the chip stays deselected and in power-down until a design drives them.

### MRAM

A 128 KB non-volatile SPI memory (Everspin MR25H10CDF) that keeps its contents without power and has no write wear: settings, logs, a boot menu, a save file. CS is pulled up so the chip stays deselected while power comes up (datasheet section 4); WP and HOLD are pulled up and not connected to the FPGA, so writes are allowed and transfers never pause. The exposed pad is ground only, with two vias under it. Four bank 14 lines at 3.3 V.

| R154 | 10k | 10k resistor from MRAM_CS to +3V3, for U33 (SPI MRAM): keeps the MRAM deselected and tracking VDD during power-up (datasheet section 4) |
| R155 | 10k | 10k resistor from MRAM_WP to +3V3, for U33 (SPI MRAM): write protect released: writes to the status register allowed |
| R156 | 10k | 10k resistor from MRAM_HOLD to +3V3, for U33 (SPI MRAM): hold released: transfers never pause |

### microSD socket

A push-push microSD socket (Hroparts TF-01A) wired for SPI mode: chip select on DAT3, data in on CMD, data out on DAT0, clock on CLK, five bank 14 lines at 3.3 V including the card-detect switch. The 10k pull-ups hold CS, the two data lines and the two unused DAT lines high, as the SD specification asks for SPI mode; the 100 nF and 10 uF feed the card's supply at the socket; the shell is grounded. Cheap removable storage for a soft CPU: a filesystem, images to load into the PSRAMs, logs.

### PSRAM0 power-up state

Six 10k resistors at the PSRAM0 pins: CE# pulled up to its own supply, clock and the four data lines pulled down. The chip requires these levels from the first moment of its supply ramp until 150 us after it, and an unconfigured FPGA leaves its pins floating, so resistors, not the FPGA, guarantee them (APS6404L section 8, findings 39).

## Supervisor

The RP2350B board controller: USB, power sequencing, programming the FPGA.

### U7  board controller

The board controller, a Raspberry Pi RP2350B microcontroller that is always on. It is what the USB cable talks to: it loads designs into the FPGA over JTAG or writes them to the FPGA's flash, turns the supplies on in order and watches them, asks a USB-PD charger for 9 V, enables extension power, and gives the FPGA a debug and UART link. One 100 nF capacitor per supply pin (RP-008280 section 2.2.1).

### USB-PD sink

Negotiates the supply voltage with a USB-PD charger. Out of the box it asks for 5 V: CFG1 is pulled up to the chip's own 3.3 V and CFG2/CFG3 are grounded, so the only other request the pins can form is 9 V, which the board controller selects by turning Q3 on (PD_REQ_9V). A dead or resetting controller leaves it at 5 V. PD_PG tells the controller whether the charger agreed.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 | BSS138LT1G | 9 V request switch: Small N-MOSFET the board controller (PD_REQ_9V) uses to pull the CH224K's CFG1 low and ask the charger for 9 V. Off: 5 V. |
| U18 | CH224K | USB-PD negotiator: WCH CH224K: asks a USB-PD charger for 5 V by default, or 9 V when the board controller turns Q3 on. Its pins cannot form any higher request. |
| C137 | 1uF | 1uF bypass on PD_VDD, for U18 (USB-PD negotiator): CH224K's internal regulator output |
| R11 | 10k | 10k pull-up of PD_PG to +3V3, for U7 (board controller): CH224K: high when the charger accepted the request |
| R172 | 10k | 10k resistor from PD_CFG1 to PD_VDD, for U18 (USB-PD negotiator): CH224K request: high (pull-up) = 5 V, pulled low by Q3 = 9 V; CH224K's internal regulator output |
| R173 | 100k | 100k resistor from PD_REQ_9V to GND, for U7 (board controller): Q3's gate; off (5 V) unless the board controller drives it high |

### JTAG owner selection

Decides who programs the FPGA over JTAG. Normally (J52 open) the board controller does, through the U20 switch. Fit a jumper on J52 and U20 disconnects the board controller completely, so an external programmer plugged into J2 has the FPGA to itself. A jumper, not software, so it works even when the board controller is broken.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| J52 | PZ254V-11-02P | EXT JTAG jumper: Fit a shunt to hand the FPGA's JTAG to an external programmer on J2. |
| U20 | SN74CB3Q3384APWR | JTAG switch: TI SN74CB3Q3384 bus switch: connects or isolates the board controller's JTAG from the FPGA, set by J52. |
| C138 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +3V3, for U20 (JTAG switch) |
| R33 | 0 | 0 series resistor between JTAG_TDO and JTAG_TDO_SW, for U20 (JTAG switch): probe point between the FPGA's TDO and U20 |
| R34 | 10k | 10k resistor from EXTERNAL_JTAG_SELECTED to GND, for U20 (JTAG switch): high when J52 is fitted: U20 disconnects the board controller |

|---|---|---|

| D11 | F.0603.00025/P2-0603G1TS2-06T-002 | USER 2 LED: Green LED for software use. |

## Slots

The ten extension ports: connectors, per-slot fuses, 5 V level shifting.

### 5V BUS 0 converter

Lets the FPGA (3.3 V) talk to 5 V extensions on slot L. U9 shifts eight lines between 3.3 V and 5 V, all in one direction at a time (BUS5V0_DIR). It stays off until the FPGA pulls BUS5V0_OE_N low; the pull-up keeps the bus off while the FPGA is still loading.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| U9 | SN74LXC8T245PWR | 5V BUS 0 translator: TI SN74LXC8T245: 8-bit 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter with direction control, for slot L. |
| C139 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +1V8_IO, for U9 (5V BUS 0 translator) |
| C140 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +5V, for U9 (5V BUS 0 translator) |
| R96 | 10k | 10k pull-up of BUS5V0_OE_N to +1V8_IO, for U9 (5V BUS 0 translator): keeps the 5 V bus translator disabled until the FPGA enables it |

### 5V BUS 1 converter

Same as 5V BUS 0, for slot M: U10 shifts eight lines between the FPGA's 3.3 V and 5 V, direction BUS5V1_DIR, off until BUS5V1_OE_N goes low.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| U10 | SN74LXC8T245PWR | 5V BUS 1 translator: TI SN74LXC8T245: 8-bit 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter with direction control, for slot M. |
| C141 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +1V8_IO, for U10 (5V BUS 1 translator) |
| C142 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +5V, for U10 (5V BUS 1 translator) |
| R97 | 10k | 10k pull-up of BUS5V1_OE_N to +1V8_IO, for U10 (5V BUS 1 translator): keeps the 5 V bus translator disabled until the FPGA enables it |

### SLOT L branches

Power for whatever is plugged into slot L. The 1x7 power socket carries PIN V (3.3 V), 3.3 V, 5 V and AUX, each beside a ground, and each through its own resettable fuse, so a short on one extension trips only that slot's fuse and the rest of the board keeps running. The long grounded pin in front of the socket is the key that stops an extension going in the wrong way, and a ground probe point.

## Network

Gigabit Ethernet (PHY and jack) and the two raw LVDS link ports.

### U30  gigabit PHY

U30 is the Ethernet PHY: it turns the FPGA's RGMII bus (four data bits each way plus clock and control, 2.5 V, bank 16) into 1000Base-T signals on the ETH jack's four twisted pairs. The FPGA still needs a MAC; the PHY handles the line, link negotiation and the analog side. It runs from +3V3, takes its RGMII pad supply from +2V5 and makes its own 1.0 V core supply with an internal LDO (the FD variant, so no inductor). The capacitors here bypass those supplies (RTL8211F datasheet rev 1.7, Table 9).

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| U30 | RTL8211FD-CG | gigabit Ethernet PHY: Realtek RTL8211FD-CG: 10/100/1000Base-T transceiver between the FPGA's RGMII bus and the ETH jack. Managed over MDIO from the FPGA; reset and interrupt on bank 35 at 3.3 V. |

### PHY straps and LEDs

Resistors that configure U30 at reset and drive its LEDs. During reset the PHY reads the level on several output pins as configuration: PHY address 1, PLL kept running, 2 ns clock delays on both RGMII directions (so the FPGA needs none), and an external 2.5 V I/O supply (RTL8211F Tables 10 and 11). The same LED pins later drive the jack's LEDs, whose polarity follows the strap (section 7.9, Figure 5). Also here: the reset pull-down that holds the PHY in reset until the FPGA is configured, the interrupt and MDIO pull-ups. Full table: ref/network.md.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|

| R133 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of PHY_INT_N to +3V3, for U30 (gigabit Ethernet PHY): U30's open-drain interrupt (Table 4) |
| R134 | 1.5k | 1.5k pull-up of PHY_MDIO to +2V5, for U30 (gigabit Ethernet PHY): MDIO idle-high pull-up, 1.5 k (section 7.11.2) |
| R135 | 4.7k | 4.7k pull-up of PHY_RXD3 to +2V5, for U30 (gigabit Ethernet PHY): strap PHYAD0 = 1: PHY address 1 (Table 10) |

### ETH jack

The Ethernet connector, with the 1000Base-T transformers and two LEDs built into the jack. The transformers isolate the cable from the board; the capacitor returns their centre taps to ground (ref/network.md).

| C243 | 100nF 50V | 100nF 50V capacitor from ETH_CT to GND, for J70 (ETH jack): returns the jack's transformer centre taps to ground ([verify] ref/network.md) |

### PHY clock

The 25 MHz crystal U30 needs as its reference (RTL8211F Table 56: 25 MHz, +/-50 ppm all in). The two capacitors set the crystal's load; the 0 ohm resistor is a placeholder to limit crystal drive if measurement shows it needs it.

| C244 | 18pF | 18 pF load capacitor on the crystal's input side (X3, CL 12 pF with about 3 pF stray: 2 x (12 - 3)) |
| C245 | 18pF | 18 pF load capacitor on the crystal's output side (X3) |
| R146 | 0 | 0 ohm in series with U30's crystal drive pin: a spot to fit a resistor if the measured drive level exceeds 0.5 mW (Table 56) |

### LINK P

A board-to-board link port, not Ethernet. Four LVDS pairs from FPGA bank 16 go straight to an RJ45 so two boards can be cabled with shielded twisted pair: a clock and a data pair out, a clock and a data pair in. Cable LINK P of one board to LINK Q of the other, and power both boards before plugging in (ref/link-ports.md). The two arrays clamp ESD at the jack.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| D20 | TPD4E1U06DBVR | LINK P ESD, pins 1-2 and 3-6: TI TPD4E1U06 four-line ESD clamp (0.8 pF) on LINK P's outgoing clock and data pairs. |
| D21 | TPD4E1U06DBVR | LINK P ESD, pins 4-5 and 7-8: TI TPD4E1U06 four-line ESD clamp (0.8 pF) on LINK P's incoming clock and data pairs. |
| J71 | LINK P | LINK P jack: Plain shielded RJ45 (no magnetics) carrying four LVDS pairs of link port P. Not an Ethernet port. |

### LINK Q

The second link port, wired as the mirror of LINK P so a straight cable from a P to a Q connects outputs to inputs. Same rules: STP cable, power both boards first (ref/link-ports.md).

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| D22 | TPD4E1U06DBVR | LINK Q ESD, pins 1-2 and 3-6: TI TPD4E1U06 four-line ESD clamp (0.8 pF) on LINK Q's incoming clock and data pairs. |
| D23 | TPD4E1U06DBVR | LINK Q ESD, pins 4-5 and 7-8: TI TPD4E1U06 four-line ESD clamp (0.8 pF) on LINK Q's outgoing clock and data pairs. |
| J72 | LINK Q | LINK Q jack: Plain shielded RJ45 (no magnetics) carrying four LVDS pairs of link port Q, mirrored from P. Not an Ethernet port. |

## Video

HDMI output straight from the FPGA, with its protection chip.

### HDMI out

A video output for monitors and TVs. Bank 35 drives the four HDMI lanes directly as TMDS_33 pairs, the standard Artix-7 way: the monitor's own 50 ohm pull-ups to 3.3 V terminate them, so the board adds none. 720p at 60 Hz fits comfortably; 1080p at 60 Hz does not. U31 sits at the connector: it clamps ESD on every line, shifts the DDC (EDID) and CEC lines between 3.3 V and the cable's 5 V, buffers hot plug, and feeds the cable's 5 V pin through a 55 mA current limit (TI SLLSE96F, Figure 18). Its two enables are pulled on, so EDID works under any design. The unused utility pin goes to ground through 75 ohm, as TI's layout example asks.

| Ref | Value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| J73 | HDMI OUT | HDMI OUT jack: Amphenol 10029449 HDMI type A socket: video out from FPGA bank 35, DVI-compatible, 720p60 and below. |

| C248 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on +5V, for U31 (HDMI protection and level shifter) |
| C249 | 100nF | 100nF bypass on HDMI_5V, for U31 (HDMI protection and level shifter) |
